entries.title: Draft: critical survival as a pivotal-measure atom
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. On any infinite connected locally finite graph with Bernoulli bond critical parameter 0<p_c<1, the finite positive measures mu_n(dp)=f_n'(p)dp on [0,p_c], where f_n(p)=P_p(o connects inside B(o,n) to its sphere), converge weakly to theta_o(p_c) delta_{p_c}. No argument excluding the limiting critical atom on the full quasi-transitive target.

entries.title: Draft: exact critical-window integrability criterion
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. Under L02's assumptions, theta_o(p_c)=0 iff lim_{delta down to 0} sup_n integral_{p_c-delta}^{p_c} f_n'(p)dp=0. A uniform L^r bound on f_n' in a fixed left neighbourhood of p_c, for any r>1, is sufficient. Establish critical-window uniform integrability using quasi-transitivity, especially on Z^3. The iff criterion is a reduction equivalent to the full target, not a proof of it.
assumptions: For the sufficient criterion only: eta in (0,p_c), r>1, and sup_n ||f_n'||_{L^r([p_c-eta,p_c])}<infinity

entries.title: Draft: degree-eight tree with positive critical survival
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. The rooted spherically symmetric tree with k_n=floor(log_2((n+1)^2)) and b_n=2^(1+k_n-k_{n-1}) children at level n-1 is connected, locally finite, has maximum degree 8, is not quasi-transitive, and has Bernoulli bond p_c=1/2 with theta_root(p_c)>=6/pi^2. This is outside the quasi-transitive target and does not solve it; it identifies a necessary symmetry-dependent step.
assumptions: Independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the specified deterministic tree

entries.title: Unproved route input: quasi-transitive critical-window bound
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT IN THIS PACKET; worldwide status UNKNOWN. Every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with 0<p_c<1 satisfies critical-window uniform integrability (UI_c) for its finite-radius Russo pivotal sums. Unproved: derive UI_c from symmetry in the residual subexponential-growth class. Local pivotal limits and bounded total L^1 mass do not suffice.
assumptions: Infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph

entries.title: Draft: pointwise derivative limits can lose a critical atom
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For the tree in L04 and the root-to-level-n event, f_n'(p)<=n(2p)^n(n+1)^2/p ->0 for every p in (0,1/2), whereas integral_0^{1/2} f_n'(p)dp>=6/pi^2 for every n. The construction is not quasi-transitive; the symmetry-dependent critical-window estimate remains unproved.

entries.title: Draft: uniform finite-radius pivotal bound on regular trees
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the D-regular tree, D>=3, put b=D-1 and c_b=(b-1)/(2b)(1-1/b)^(b-2). Then p_c=1/b and every finite-radius root-to-sphere probability satisfies sup_{p in [1/(2b),1/b]} f_n'(p)<=D(1+2/c_b). For D=3 the uniform upper bound is 27. The same bound is not established for the residual subexponential quasi-transitive target; G01 remains unproved.

entries.title: Draft: mass transport leaves the distant-centre tail
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. On a locally finite transitive graph satisfying the mass-transport principle, the finite-radius Russo influence I_n(p) for the root-to-sphere event equals (1/2) sum_u sum_{e incident to o} P_p(e pivotal for the radius-n event centred at u). Mass transport does not bound the sum over all distant centres uniformly in n or in a critical window; G01 remains unproved. No formula is claimed on a nonunimodular graph without weights.
assumptions: Mass-transport principle for nonnegative diagonally invariant transports

entries.title: Draft: strengthened regular-tree derivative bound 12
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the D-regular tree, D>=3, let b=D-1 and c_b=(b-1)/(2b)(1-1/b)^(b-2). For every n>=1, sup_{p in [0,1/b]} f_n'(p)<=D/c_b. For D=3 the bound is 12, strengthening L06's bound 27 on a smaller interval. Regular-tree special case only; G01 on the full quasi-transitive class remains unproved. Discovery credited to w433; w432 independently rederived the bound. Referee w434 pending.

entries.title: Draft scope correction: the lattice is a special case of the graph target
entries.statement: DRAFT SOURCE CORRECTION, independent review pending. The assertion of critical Bernoulli bond extinction on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph G with p_c(G)<1 includes the nearest-neighbour Z^d case under the same critical-parameter restriction. A proof only on Z^d does not by itself cover all polynomial-growth quasi-transitive graphs. The cited prior attempt supplies no converse reduction; retain the valid one-way specialization rather than an equivalence.
assumptions: The general graph target is read with its full stated hypotheses

relations.rationale: The limiting critical-window mass is the critical survival atom; the exact iff proof is in L03.
The pointwise derivative obstruction uses the specified degree-eight tree and its positive critical survival.
The tree exhibits a nonzero critical atom despite pointwise subcritical derivative decay.
The counterexample fails quasi-transitivity and shows why independent bonds and bounded degree alone cannot prove the proposed critical-window estimate.
The proved regular-tree L-infinity influence bound verifies the sufficient integrability criterion for this subclass.
Under the explicitly assumed mass-transport principle, the critical-window mass equals the integrated incoming pivotal mass over all centres.
The stronger D/c_b bound on the whole interval [0,1/b] implies the old D(1+2/c_b) bound on [1/(2b),1/b]. For D=3 the constants are 12 and 27 respectively.
G01 is the unproved critical-window input identified by the exact target-equivalence criterion; the parent target is not proved.
Both concern the scope of the full quasi-transitive target; neither is a proof of that target.
